reasons: Deviation classification is supported: the cited text commits IBM to a three-year term with automatic renewal (p0104/p0658) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause, so there is no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term — squarely the rule's walk-away scenario, failing both preferred (30 days) and fallback (60–90 days with capped fee).

The rationale correctly disposes of the near-miss alternatives (six/twelve-month non-renewal notice bites only at term end; SOW 6.1 PO cancellation is order-level and cost-reimbursable), so this is not an acceptable-fallback clause being over-upgraded.

The inserted language reaches the preferred position with a targeted addition: 30 days' written notice, no termination penalty, refund of prepaid amounts, and an express bar on MSL terminating for convenience mid-term; it is an insert rather than a rewrite, so no unnecessary disturbance of surrounding text.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check is a phrasing artifact ('for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice') rather than a substantive gap — the Customer convenience right is plainly granted.

Carve-out for amounts payable under Sections 5.2/5.3 is a reasonable manufacturing-inventory concession (payment for goods, not an early-termination penalty) and does not fall below the fallback; the comment accurately describes the change and cites the playbook position.
Minor nit only (not a fail): the inserted clause is described as 'Section 5.4' in the rationale but the rendered text carries no section number, so the numbering should be added on execution.
